definition: Ollama is an open-source software platform developed by Jeffrey Morgan and Michael Chiang in 2023 for running and managing large language models on local GPU infrastructure and through hosted cloud models.
details: It provides a command-line interface, a native GUI, a local REST API, model-management tools, and integrations for using open-weight models with coding assistants and other applications.

explainer.lead: How to install Ollama, a first working example, and where it fits in an AI project.
explainer.createdBy: Created by Jeffrey Morgan and Michael Chiang (Ollama, Inc.), 2023.

install.python: pip install ollama   # plus the Ollama app from ollama.com

quickstart.python:
import ollama

# first:  ollama pull llama3.2
reply = ollama.chat(model="llama3.2", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Why is the sky blue?"}])
print(reply.message.content)

explainer.inAi: Run open models locally for private prototyping; a Modelfile lets you set a system prompt and parameters for your own named model.

tiers.eli5: Like an app store and player for AI models that you run on your own computer instead of someone else's server.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use its command-line interface, native GUI, local REST API, and model-management tools to download, run, import, and manage models, and integrate them with coding assistants and other applications.
tiers.paperLevel: No formal definition; it is a software platform whose interface is a CLI, GUI, local REST API, and model-management tooling, and whose models run on local GPU infrastructure or as hosted cloud models.

explainer.example: A developer pulls an open-weight model with Ollama and calls it through the local REST API from a coding assistant on the same machine.
